headline: 311 extremists from banned groups are fugitive in Bangladesh
summary: Anti-Terrorism Unit data reveals hundreds of militants are on the run, while others were released on bail or escaped during recent unrest.
details: According to the Anti-Terrorism Unit (ATU), 311 members of seven banned extremist organizations are currently fugitive. Additionally, 59 members of Hizb ut-Tahrir are also in hiding.

The fugitives include 185 members of Jamaatul Mujahideen Bangladesh (JMB), 83 from Ansar al-Islam, 16 from Harkat-ul-Jihad al-Islami Bangladesh (HuJI-B), 16 from Neo-JMB, 9 from Allah's Army, and individuals from Jamaatul Ansar fil Hind al-Sharqiya and Imam Mahmud's convoy.

Security analysts warn that these fugitives, along with those released on bail or who escaped from prison, pose a significant security risk. Concerns are heightened as many firearms looted from police stations and prisons during the July 2024 uprising remain unrecovered.
On August 5, 2024, 202 prisoners, including 9 extremists, escaped from the Kashimpur High Security Central Jail after attackers broke the main gate and set fire to a warehouse.

ATU data shows that between 2021 and 2024, 2,143 members of banned extremist groups were arrested nationwide. However, 1,611 were released on bail between 2021 and December 2025, with 380 released after the August 5 uprising.
Currently, 16 prisons across the country hold 59 death row convicts, 46 life prisoners, and 25 others serving various terms from these organizations. Another 32 prisoners are awaiting trial.

Notable figures such as Jasim Uddin Rahmani, leader of Ansarullah Bangla Team, and Maulana Saidur Rahman, head of JMB, have been released on bail recently. Some suspects in the Keraniganj madrasa explosion were also briefly released before being re-arrested.
Law enforcement officials emphasize that surveillance of these individuals is critical to prevent a return to the violence seen between 2013 and 2016, including the 2016 Holey Artisan Bakery attack.

headline_marked: Singer [[Mirza Tanjim Sharif Mugdho becomes Executive Magistrate]]
headline: Singer Mirza Tanjim Sharif Mugdho becomes Executive Magistrate
summary: Former 'Sera Kontho' champion and BUET engineer, Mirza Tanjim Sharif Mugdho, ranks in the top 50 of the 47th BCS results for the administration cadre.
details: Mirza Tanjim Sharif Mugdho, once known as the champion of Channel i Sera Kontho, has entered the administration cadre of the 47th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examination.
He ranked within the top 50 in the merit list, earning a recommendation for the position of Assistant Commissioner and Executive Magistrate.
Mugdho shared the news on Facebook, expressing gratitude for the success despite the pressures of his professional life as a lecturer at a private university in Dhaka since 2019.
A lifelong high-achiever, Mugdho earned GPA 5.00 in both secondary and higher secondary education at Mymensingh Zilla School and Notre Dame College.
He is a BUET graduate in engineering and has won 29 national awards before entering university, including being a six-time national mathematics olympiad champion.
In 2012, he earned an 'Honorable Mention' at the 53rd International Mathematical Olympiad in Argentina.
Born in Mymensingh, he is the son of a college teacher and a health inspector. He is the second of three brothers.
From the Sera Kontho stage to the administration cadre, Mugdho is now starting a new chapter of his life with a commitment to honesty and responsibility.
caption:
From singing champion to Executive Magistrate! 🎤

Mirza Tanjim Sharif Mugdho ranks in the top 50 of the 47th BCS.

Mirza Tanjim Sharif Mugdho, once known as the champion of Channel i Sera Kontho, has entered the administration cadre of the 47th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examination.

He ranked within the top 50 in the merit list, earning a recommendation for the position of Assistant Commissioner and Executive Magistrate.

Mugdho shared the news on Facebook, expressing gratitude for the success despite the pressures of his professional life as a lecturer at a private university in Dhaka since 2019.

A lifelong high-achiever, Mugdho earned GPA 5.00 in both secondary and higher secondary education at Mymensingh Zilla School and Notre Dame College.

He is a BUET graduate in engineering and has won 29 national awards before entering university, including being a six-time national mathematics olympiad champion.

In 2012, he earned an 'Honorable Mention' at the 53rd International Mathematical Olympiad in Argentina.

Born in Mymensingh, he is the son of a college teacher and a health inspector. He is the second of three brothers.

From the Sera Kontho stage to the administration cadre, Mugdho is now starting a new chapter of his life with a commitment to honesty and responsibility.
